ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is a pentagon, with vertices in clockwise order (or along the edges) successively A-B-C-D-E. The side lengths marked on the figure are AB=16, BC=14, CD=17, DE=13, EA=14. Reasoning: Let the radii of the five circles with A, B, C, D, E as centers respectively be r_A, r_B, r_C, r_D, r_E. The problem statement says that the two circles whose centers are the endpoints of each side are tangent on that side, so the sum of the radii of two adjacent circles equals the corresponding side length: r_A+r_B=16, r_B+r_C=14, r_C+r_D=17, r_D+r_E=13, r_E+r_A=14. From r_B=16-r_A, get r_C=14-r_B=r_A-2; then get r_D=17-r_C=19-r_A; then get r_E=13-r_D=r_A-6. Substitute into r_E+r_A=14, obtaining (r_A-6)+r_A=14, so 2r_A=20, r_A=10. Thus r_B=6, r_C=8, r_D=9, r_E=4. The largest radius is 10, corresponding to center A.
